/-!
# Erdős Problem 646

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/646](https://www.erdosproblems.com/646)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
- [Be97] Berend, Daniel, *On the parity of exponents in the factorization of $n!$*.
  J. Number Theory (1997), 13-19.
-/

open scoped Nat

namespace Erdos646

/--
Let $p_1,\ldots,p_k$ be distinct primes. Are there infinitely many $n$ such that $n!$ is
divisible by an even power of each of the $p_i$?

The answer is yes, proved by Berend [Be97], who further proved that the sequence of such $n$
has bounded gaps (where the bound depends on the initial set of primes).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos646.lean"]
theorem erdos_646 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ p ∈ S, p.Prime) →
      {n : ℕ | ∀ p ∈ S, Even (padicValNat p (n !))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos646

reformulations.difference: Distinct primes are represented by a Finset rather than an indexed family. The Lean statement also permits the empty prime set and n = 0, unlike a presentation restricted to nonempty families and positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Enumerating a Finset by Fin S.card produces an injective family; conversely, the image of an injective finite family is a Finset with the same conditions. The empty-family case gives all natural numbers, and deleting n = 0 does not change infinitude. The complete equivalence with the indexed formulation restricted to k > 0 and n > 0 was proved as positive_indexed_source_form_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Erdős and Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), pp. 76–79, especially p. 77; scanned book read using OCR: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf

https://www.jams.jp/notice/mj/46-3.html (publisher's contents confirming Erdős 1997, pp. 527–537; no full text supplied)

review.notes:
The website records PROVED (LEAN), agreeing with answer(True), research solved, and the formal_proof attribution. ErGr80 p. 77 explicitly concerns even exponents in the prime decomposition, supporting the exact-valuation interpretation. Primality and factorial positivity exclude padicValNat's problematic default cases. Scratch checks covered empty sets, n = 0 and 1, concrete satisfying and nonsatisfying instances, and equivalence with exact even-power divisibility.

The linked proof's main dependency fragment and a translation to the exact repository proposition were kernel-checked in /workspace/review/verified-external-proof.lean, after two tactic-only compatibility adjustments for the newer installed toolchain. Both use only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

Full texts of Be97 and Er97e could not be retrieved; their bibliographic entries were checked. The declaration's faithfulness was settled using the website's exact LaTeX statement and the original book passage. The reviewed file was not modified.
